Severe Flooding Disrupts Bahraini Trade and Infrastructure, Economic Impact Mounts

Severe flooding across Bahrain is causing widespread disruption to trade, logistics, and infrastructure, with economic impacts mounting as the situation continues to unfold. Torrential rainfall over the past 48 hours has inundated key transport routes, industrial zones, and residential districts, prompting the government to declare a state of emergency.

Authorities report that the central and northern governorates are among the hardest hit, with the main commercial port at Mina Salman operating at reduced capacity due to waterlogged access roads. “We are working around the clock to restore essential services, but the volume of water has overwhelmed our drainage systems,” said Yousif Al-Mansoori, spokesperson for the Ministry of Works.

The Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry has called for urgent measures to protect critical supply chains. “Many wholesalers and retailers are unable to receive shipments, and disruptions are rippling across the market,” said Fatima Al-Khalifa, head of the chamber’s logistics committee.

Floodwaters have forced several industrial estates in Sitra and Hidd to suspend operations, with the Bahraini Federation of Manufacturers estimating that as much as 40% of factories in affected areas are currently idle. “We are concerned about the long-term damage to equipment and facilities,” said the federation’s chairman.

Analysts warn that prolonged flooding could dampen Bahrain’s projected GDP growth for the year. “The immediate priority is to restore transport links, but the economic aftershocks will likely be felt for months,” said Ahmed Jawad, senior economist at Gulf Insights Research.

The Meteorological Directorate has warned that further heavy rain is expected in the coming days, raising concerns about additional disruption and economic losses.
